# Refined Cost Segregation

> Engineering-based, ATG-aligned cost segregation studies, reviewed by a licensed tax professional, for 1-4 unit residential property, including short-term rentals (STR) and long-term rentals (LTR). Serves clients across the United States. No site visits required; the methodology is documentary, working from closing statements, photos, and structured intake.

## About

Refined Cost Segregation is a residential-specialty cost segregation firm built by tax and real estate professionals. Every study is reviewed and signed off by a qualified licensed tax professional.

The firm exists to make defensible, audit-ready cost segregation accessible to the 1-4 unit residential investor market that traditional commercial cost-seg firms serve poorly or charge disproportionately for. Pricing is a transparent, formula-based fixed fee, quoted per property from the intake form or a call rather than published. Optional Audit Support is available in Basic (first-claim year, exams within 3 years) and Extended (any affected year, exams within 10 years) levels. Over 12 units, 1031 exchanges, and carryover-basis situations are quoted manually.

## Key facts (current as of 2026)

- 100% bonus depreciation was restored for property acquired after January 19, 2025, by the One Big Beautiful Bill (OBBB), signed mid-2025. No scheduled sunset.
- A typical residential cost segregation study reclassifies 20-35% of depreciable basis into 5-, 7-, and 15-year property; short-term rentals typically reclassify higher, around 32%+.
- For STRs with an average customer-use period of 7 days or less, IRS Treasury Regulation §1.469-1T(e)(3) treats the activity as a non-rental trade or business. Material participation (any of the IRS's 7 tests) makes the resulting losses non-passive and usable against W-2 income.
- Turnaround: 5-10 business days from complete intake to delivered PDF report.

## Methodology and language

- "Audit-ready, ATG-aligned, reviewed by a licensed tax professional," never "audit-proof," which overpromises and isn't accurate.
- Engineering-based methodology, prepared to the IRS Audit Technique Guide for residential property.
- Documentary process; no site visits required for 1-4 unit residential.
- Always works alongside the client's CPA, never replaces or poaches.

## Journal essays

- [The short-term rental loophole, explained without the YouTube fluff.](https://www.refinedcostseg.com/journal/short-term-rental-loophole.html) (May 2026). Covers the IRC §469 mechanic that lets STR owners deduct losses against W-2 income, the four most relevant material participation tests, the contemporaneous documentation requirement, and the realistic scenarios where the math pencils.
